title: Check: HA control planes
description: Five questions on removing the single point of failure.

questions.prompt: What are the two kubeadm HA topologies?
questions.explanation: Stacked puts etcd on the control plane nodes; external runs it on its own machines, at the cost of more hosts.

questions.prompt: How many control plane nodes should an HA cluster have?
questions.explanation: The constraint comes from etcd's Raft quorum. Three tolerates one failure; two tolerates none.

questions.prompt: What sits in front of the API servers?

options.text: A load balancer on port 6443, whose address is the control plane endpoint

questions.explanation: `--control-plane-endpoint` must point at that load balancer at init time, or you cannot add control plane nodes later.

questions.prompt: A three-node stacked cluster loses two control plane nodes. What is the state?

options.text: etcd has no quorum, so the API server cannot serve writes

questions.explanation: Without quorum, no writes. Existing Pods keep running - the data plane does not depend on the control plane.

questions.prompt: How do the scheduler and controller manager behave with several control plane nodes?

options.text: They elect a leader; only one is active

questions.explanation: Leader election prevents two schedulers from binding the same Pod twice.
